title: Lumenary Statistics
subtitle: Statistics from averages and charts to Bayesian computation, causal inference and the statistics of AI in 2026: statistical thinking, models, modern inference, advanced methods and the frontier.
description: Lumenary Statistics is a subject of Lumenary Scientia, free and open source like the others. Statistics is the science of learning from data in the presence of variation and uncertainty — a discipline of its own, with its own questions and habits of mind, not just a branch of mathematics. The course starts with no experience at all — what an average hides and how graphs mislead — and climbs through distributions and sampling, estimation and testing, regression and experimental design, Bayesian and computational inference, causal inference, time series, survival and multilevel models, to the statistics of machine learning and AI as practised in 2026.

Every lesson teaches with ideas first and calculation second. Simulations and analyses are in Python with NumPy and SciPy (pandas where data tables help), and every block with a **Run in browser** button runs there, with nothing to install. A lesson says *Code tested* only when all of its code passed. Lumenary Statistics relies on [Lumenary Math](/en/math/) for probability and links to its lessons; Lumenary CS's [Data Science](/en/cs/electives/data-science/) elective puts these methods to work.

Every lesson was drafted with AI assistance and is awaiting review by a human statistician. The text, exercises and code are original and licensed CC BY-SA 4.0 (code Apache-2.0). Where a statistical society, agency or research group has published the primary source, the lesson links to it rather than retelling it.

levels.title: Making sense of data
levels.summary: No experience needed, from about age 11. What statistics is for, describing data with numbers and pictures, chance and probability, samples and surveys, and how statistics can mislead.

levels.title: Statistical thinking
levels.summary: The core ideas of inference: distributions, sampling distributions and the central limit theorem, estimation and confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and comparing groups.

levels.title: Statistical models
levels.summary: Models that relate variables: linear and multiple regression, generalised linear models, experimental design and analysis of variance, and likelihood and model selection.

levels.title: Modern inference
levels.summary: How statisticians reason today: Bayesian inference, Markov chain Monte Carlo, resampling and simulation, and multiple testing and reproducibility.

levels.title: Advanced methods
levels.summary: Methods for the questions real data raise: causal inference, time series, survival analysis, multilevel models, and high-dimensional statistics.

levels.title: The frontier of statistics
levels.summary: Where statistics meets machine learning and society in 2026: statistical learning theory, conformal prediction, causal machine learning, the statistics of evaluating AI, and privacy and official statistics.
